newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria expects to raise domestic gas sales.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria expects to raise domestic gas sales.

text.p: Nigeria is to sell 130 billion standard cubic feet of gas locally in 1997 compared with 123 billion in 1996, a senior gas official said.

"We have projected a sales volume of 130 billion standard cubic feet of gas this year going by the increasing demand in the domestic market," Jackson Gaius-Obaseki, managing director of the Nigerian Gas Company, told reporters in the midwestern oil town of Warri on Saturday.
His company is a subsidiary of state oil giant NNPC.
Nigeria has huge gas reserves but 75 percent is currently flared in the production of crude oil.
Gaius-Obaseki said the company had begun supplying 12 million standard cubic feet of gas per day to the aluminium smelter plant in Akwa Ibom state in the southeast.
It would also start supplying 50 million standard cubic feet of gas per day to industries in the Lagos area before the end of the year, he added.
The state power firm, the National Electric Power Authority, remains the biggest consumer of gas in the country.
Industry experts argue that low pricing for gas is a disincentive for potential investors in the gas business.
Gaius-Obaseki said his company hoped to participate in a project to pipe Nigerian gas to some of its West African neighbours.
"We may be involved either through direct participation in the West African Pipeline Company or indirectly as a carrier of the gas through our pipeline system," he said.
